# Command reference

<!-- Generated by `go generate ./skills` from the command tree. Do not edit. -->

Every `indexit` command in this release with its flags, as `--help` shows them.
Every command also accepts `-h, --help`.

## indexit

```text
indexit [command]
```

Global flags, accepted by every command in any position:

- `--env-file string`: path to .env file (default: auto-discover; pass "" to disable)
- `--heartbeat duration`: emit a 'still waiting...' line if a network call exceeds this duration (0 disables) (default 10s)
- `-q, --quiet`: suppress everything below error level (stdout payload unaffected)
- `-v, --verbose count`: increase log verbosity (-v debug, -vvv enables gotd internals)

## indexit telegram

Fetch Telegram dialogs and message history

```text
indexit telegram [command]
```

Flags of every `indexit telegram` command:

- `--peer-cache string`: path to Telegram peer cache file
- `--session string`: path to Telegram session file
- `--timeout string`: wall-clock timeout for Telegram operations (default "0")

## indexit telegram auth

Manage Telegram authentication

```text
indexit telegram auth [command]
```

## indexit telegram auth login

Run interactive Telegram login

```text
indexit telegram auth login [flags]
```

Flags:

- `--qr`: log in by scanning a QR code from a logged-in device (no phone code needed)

## indexit telegram auth logout

Invalidate Telegram session and remove local session file

```text
indexit telegram auth logout
```

## indexit telegram auth status

Print Telegram session status

```text
indexit telegram auth status
```

## indexit telegram debug

Debug Telegram helpers

```text
indexit telegram debug [command]
```

## indexit telegram debug uid

Parse a Telegram UID

```text
indexit telegram debug uid <value>
```

## indexit telegram fetch

Fetch Telegram data as JSONL

```text
indexit telegram fetch [command]
```

Flags of every `indexit telegram fetch` command:

- `--format string`: output format (default "jsonl")
- `--limit int`: maximum number of emitted records; 0 means all
- `-o, --output string`: output path, or - for stdout (default "-")
- `--page-size int`: Telegram page size (default 100)

## indexit telegram fetch dialogs

Fetch Telegram dialogs

```text
indexit telegram fetch dialogs
```

## indexit telegram fetch media

Download media of one dialog into a directory.

Files go to --dir; --output keeps its usual meaning and receives the
JSONL manifest, one record per file.

To narrow the run to one forum topic, address it as channel:<id>:<topic>.
A t.me/c/<peer>/<n> link means message <n>, not topic <n> — pasted alone
it walks the whole dialog.

```text
indexit telegram fetch media [flags]
```

Flags:

- `--dialog string` (required): dialog UID
- `--dir string` (required): destination directory for downloaded files
- `--from string`: start timestamp in RFC3339
- `--max-id int`: maximum MTProto message ID
- `--media strings`: media types to download, e.g. photo,video; empty means every downloadable type
- `--min-id int`: minimum MTProto message ID
- `--overwrite`: re-download files that already exist
- `--to string`: end timestamp in RFC3339

## indexit telegram fetch message

Fetch specific Telegram messages by ID as JSONL.

Pass message links, or --dialog with repeatable or comma-separated --id.
Links are grouped by dialog and topic in first-seen order; IDs keep their
order within each group and duplicates in that group are fetched once.
Missing, service, and out-of-scope messages are skipped with a warning.
--limit caps emitted records across all groups. Requests use at most 100 IDs;
--page-size does not apply to this command.

```text
indexit telegram fetch message [<t.me link> ...] [flags]
```

Flags:

- `--dialog string`: dialog UID (used with --id)
- `--id ints`: message ID to fetch; repeatable or comma-separated

Examples:

```sh
indexit telegram fetch message https://t.me/example_channel/11 https://t.me/example_channel/46
indexit telegram fetch message --dialog @example_channel --id 11 --id 46,47
```

## indexit telegram fetch messages

Fetch Telegram messages from one dialog

```text
indexit telegram fetch messages [flags]
```

Flags:

- `--dialog string` (required): dialog UID
- `--from string`: start timestamp in RFC3339
- `--max-id int`: maximum MTProto message ID
- `--min-id int`: minimum MTProto message ID
- `--to string`: end timestamp in RFC3339

## indexit telegram fetch peer

Fetch the cards of Telegram channels, groups, and users as JSONL.

Emits one peer record per ref, in the order of the refs. A ref is any
dialog address, a t.me/c/<id> link, or a t.me/+<hash> or t.me/joinchat/<hash>
invite link. Channels and groups are read in full: description, members,
and the linked discussion group or channel. Invite links are only
previewed: indexit never joins a chat.

A ref that cannot be parsed or fetched yields a record with an error
instead of stopping the run. The command fails only when no record was
fetched. --limit and --page-size do not apply to this command.

```text
indexit telegram fetch peer <ref>...
```

Examples:

```sh
indexit telegram fetch peer @example_channel https://t.me/example_chat
indexit telegram fetch peer channel:<id> https://t.me/+<hash>
```

## indexit telegram fetch topics

Fetch forum topics of one dialog

```text
indexit telegram fetch topics [flags]
```

Flags:

- `--dialog string` (required): dialog UID

## indexit version

Show application version.

